_README: WHICH KERNEL BOARDS ARE GATES, AND WHICH ARE DISCLOSURES.
public.fn_kernel_all_boards() discovers every board in the estate BY SIGNATURE — any
zero-argument function returning (check_name, expected, actual, ok) — so a new board is watched
the moment it is deployed and nobody has to remember to register it. Twenty-one exist today.
A board not named in this file is a GATE: every check must be ok, and any red fails the suite.
That is the default on purpose. Adding a board here is a deliberate act with a reason attached.
A board named here is a RATCHET: it is a deliberate open-gap report whose red rows are the
disclosure, not a defect to be tuned away. kernel_k6_trace_ledger.sql says so in its own header
— 'every check numerator AND denominator over the FULL table', 'the gap stays visible' — and
demanding zero there would be demanding the disclosure be deleted. What is asserted instead is
that the gap does not GROW: each listed check carries the numerator measured at baseline, and
the suite fails if the live numerator exceeds it. Debt already disclosed is allowed to stand;
new debt of the same shape is not.
kernel_boards_are_green.test.mjs also fails if a ratchet entry no longer matches a real check,
so an entry cannot outlive its subject and silently license a future failure with that name.

ratchet.why: The seven true orphan traces are preserved ON PURPOSE as the evidence of the defect they record. kernel_k6_trace_ledger.sql, section E: they are annotated with an evidence_ref stating that no task ever carried them, sealed, and deliberately counted in the open rather than filtered out of a denominator. All seven are registered in phase_c_historical_repair as HISTORICAL_ORPHAN_TRACE.

The K4 pointer defect, recorded in kernel_k6_trace_ledger.sql and classified in phase_c_historical_repair as HISTORICAL_STATE_TRACE_MISMATCH. Pre-repair rows kept rather than rewritten, because editing a sealed trace is what the append-only guard exists to refuse.
Same K4 pointer defect, handoff_run side. One row, registered.

Trace 3730, subject_kind trigger_inbox. The trace itself was never edited — fn_phase_c_trace_append_only refuses editing a sealed trace, which is correct — so its subject_kind is exactly as written. It carries an immutable repair relationship: repair_id 83 classified it, repair_id 85 superseded that classification and recorded it as a post-cutover defect that was repaired.

Counts components that have never produced a trace. 430 of the 635 are edge functions, database triggers or event subscriptions, for which this database holds no invocation log at all — fn_kernel_system_trace_state states that explicitly and declines to score them. The number is therefore a coverage-unknown figure, not a defect count, and kernel_k6 keeps it visible under section G rather than filtering it. What IS asserted, on the same board, is that 933 of 933 post-epoch wrapped cron executions carry their required trace and 0 are missing one.
ratchet.owner: open — falls as sources are cut over to the kernel and begin tracing

ratchet.why: edge:inquiry_intake. This read 0 until 18 Aug 2026, on a false basis: the source claimed discharge by routine:trg_inquiry_received, a trigger on public.inquiries, and supabase/functions/inquiry_intake/index.ts never references that table in code — only in two comments. The board resolves the named routine and verifies it reaches the kernel, which is the FAR end of the chain; it never asks whether the source reaches the routine. Correcting the claim moved this 0 -> 1, which is the true number. What the source actually writes is public.customers, a work table with no kernel discharge, and W04 has 0 runs ever. Closing it means wiring W04 — which requires reclassifying dbtrigger:public.customers:trg_emit_customer_registered away from NOT_A_BUSINESS_TRIGGER, registering a new source, and amending customer.registered.allowed_source_systems, after which every signup opens an onboarding run with an owner and an SLA. That is a founder decision, not a wiring fix.
ratchet.owner: OPEN — founder decision: should a customer registration start W04 onboarding?

ratchet.why: THE ONE OPEN PHASE C GATE. 19 of 37 active autonomous sources still start or change business work without entering the kernel. The check's own expected string says NOT MET BY K10: K10 built the door and registered the routes, and moving each source onto it is a separate wiring increment. The doors are ready — all 24 active trigger types read ADAPTER_READY_NO_LIVE_SENDER. It read 26 until the instrument was fixed: for edge functions and frontend paths, routes_through_inbox fell through to a hand-set boolean that was false on all 33 of them, so seven sources genuinely discharged by a trigger calling fn_kernel_source_emit with their source key still counted as bypassing. The view now measures that literal and consults the flag only where no routine discharges the source. 19 is what it always was. This ratchet is NOT a licence to leave it — lower it as each increment lands, and delete the entry at 0.
ratchet.owner: OPEN — 2 quote_items triggers, 2 edge functions writing customers (the W04 gap), 5 frontend paths the write map does not yet model
ratchet.measured_at: 2026-08-18, 9 of 37 (26 -> 19 when the literal-name discharge was measured; 19 -> 9 when the write map landed)

ratchet.why: PHASE D DISCLOSURE, AND IT REPLACES handlers_not_writing_a_business_object RATHER THAN JOINING IT. That entry is DELETED at 0, which is what its own text instructed: every one of the 257 handlers now calls fn_phase_d_effect_produce, every step declares one of the seven effect types, and the path from handler to business object exists and is exercised. What this NEW entry counts is a different and harder question -- how many of the 257 have actually PRODUCED their effect at least once in a recorded execution. It starts at the full 257 because the only executions so far were aborted-transaction probes, which roll back by design and leave no ledger row. It falls as D11 and D13 land per-step and per-workflow cases. A path that exists and a path that has run are not the same claim and are no longer reported by one number. Delete this entry at 0, do not lower and leave it.
ratchet.owner: OPEN -- Phase D D11/D13: run the per-step contract cases and the 30 workflow closures, each leaving a phase_d_effect_ledger row
ratchet.measured_at: 2026-08-18, 257 of 257 have never produced an effect outside an aborted transaction

ratchet.why: All 54 are step-completed events (*-S**-COMPLETED) whose emitted_by and primary_consumer_role_id are the same role in the FROZEN phase_b_event registry — a step whose successor is owned by the same role legitimately consumes its own completion. Both columns are Phase B, Phase B is frozen since 2026-08-15, and changing either needs a Phase B change request with evidence and founder approval. Phase D measured it and may not fix it. The count is left RED rather than redefined to a shape that passes, because narrowing the predicate until the number reaches zero is the rubber stamp this estate keeps finding.
ratchet.owner: OPEN — needs a Phase B change request (PBCR) to re-address the consumer of a same-owner step-completed event, or a founder ruling that a same-owner sequence is correct as designed
